rationale: Start with a broad mid-length scouting gradient covering the full solvent-strength range to reveal the retention span and whether any compounds fail to elute by 42 min. A moderate temperature helps keep viscosity and run time reasonable without overly compressing selectivity on the first injection.

All 10 compounds eluted with baseline resolution, so the opportunity is to reduce analysis time while preserving the critical cluster around peaks 5–7. A shorter full-range gradient should compress the run and test how much time can be removed before the minimum resolution begins to drop materially.

The 12 min gradient hit an excellent time score but over-compressed the critical 6/7 pair, so move slightly longer to restore resolution while likely keeping the run in the zero time-penalty region. This is a local optimization step between the successful 20 and aggressive 12 min conditions.

The trend shows the critical pair improving as gradient time increases, and 14 min is already near optimal with no time penalty. Testing 16 min should indicate whether a small additional gain in minimum resolution can push CRF even closer to 1.0 while likely remaining in the fast-run regime.

Gradient time around 14–16 min is near-optimal, so the next lever is selectivity rather than speed. Lowering temperature slightly may open the persistent 6/7 critical pair without a major time penalty, potentially improving the resolution term enough to beat the current best.

Lower temperature worsened selectivity by creating a new coelution, so probe the opposite direction while staying at the near-optimal 14 min gradient. A modest increase to 45 C may improve the critical cluster’s spacing pattern enough to raise the resolution term without sacrificing the zero time penalty.

Temperature changes hurt selectivity, so keep 40 C and instead shallow the gradient slightly by lowering the final organic fraction. This can expand the late-middle region where the critical cluster elutes, potentially improving the 6/7 separation while keeping all compounds within the no-penalty time window.

Lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the critical pair while retaining a zero time penalty, so continue in the same direction to slightly further flatten the effective gradient in the cluster region. This should test whether selectivity can be improved enough to reach the maximum CRF without pushing the last peak out of the fast window.

The best point so far is 14 min to 0.90, while 14 min to 0.85 achieved full resolution but incurred a small time penalty. Extending slightly to 16 min at 0.90 tests whether selectivity in the critical cluster can be pushed to full resolution with a smaller penalty than the 0.85 method, potentially improving on the current best.

The optimum appears to be a narrow balance between just enough spreading of the 6/7 pair and staying below the time-penalty threshold, so now test a modest increase in starting organic at the current best phi1/tG/T. Raising phi0 may subtly reshape the gradient profile around the crowded middle region and improve selectivity without greatly affecting total run time.

The move to phi0 = 0.10 improved both speed and selectivity at fixed tG/T, so combine that benefit with the earlier selectivity gain seen when lowering phi1 from 0.90 to 0.85. This should test whether the critical 6/7 pair can be fully resolved while staying close enough to the no-penalty time region to surpass the current best.

Since 0.10/0.85/14/40 reached the maximum score, the only sensible exploration is a very local neighbor to confirm whether the optimum sits on a plateau. Lowering phi1 one step should slightly increase spacing in the critical late-middle cluster, at the risk of a small time penalty.

With the maximum score already achieved, only nearby checks are worthwhile; increasing phi0 one step from the optimum will test whether the score sits on a local plateau while potentially shortening early retention a bit. This is a minimal perturbation around the proven best condition.

A second maximum at phi0 = 0.15 suggests a plateau extending toward higher starting organic, so step phi0 up once more while holding the other successful settings constant. This efficiently maps the boundary of the optimum region and may retain the maximum score with even shorter retention.

The maximum score persists at phi0 = 0.15 with phi1 = 0.85, and moving phi0 higher started to compress the critical pair, so probe the orthogonal local neighbor by raising phi1 one step. This maps the top of the apparent optimum plateau while staying close to already successful conditions.

You already have CRF 1.000, so remaining injections are best used to define the nearby optimum plateau. Lowering phi1 one step from the other 1.000 condition at phi0 = 0.15 will test whether full resolution is retained or whether time penalty appears immediately on the stronger flattening side.

With multiple 1.000 methods at 14 min, the only valuable remaining question is whether a shorter gradient can preserve full resolution and also keep zero time penalty. This directly tests whether the optimum plateau extends to a faster method near the current best composition window.

Since shortening to 12 min at phi0 = 0.10 compressed the critical pair too much, test the other 1.000 composition plateau point at phi0 = 0.15 with the same shorter gradient. The higher starting organic may preserve or improve selectivity while keeping the faster runtime.

The 12 min gradients lose critical resolution, and 14 min already reaches CRF 1.000, so the useful remaining boundary check is whether 16 min at the best composition still avoids time penalty. This maps the upper tG edge of the optimum plateau around the established best conditions.

The 16 min boundary check at phi0 = 0.10 incurred a clear time penalty, so test the same longer gradient at the other 1.000 plateau point to confirm whether that penalty is universal across the optimum region. This completes the local tG mapping around the best-performing composition family.

With the composition and time plateau mapped, the only nearby untested axis around the 1.000 optimum is temperature at the best composition. A small increase from 40 to 45 C checks whether the optimum is temperature-sensitive at phi0 0.10/phi1 0.85, complementing the earlier broader-temperature results collected at a different composition.

The 45 C test strongly degraded the critical pair at one optimum composition, so check the other 1.000 composition to confirm whether that temperature sensitivity is general across the plateau. This closes the local temperature comparison around both top-scoring methods.

The optimum clearly sits at 40 C and worsens at 45 C, so the remaining untested immediate neighbor is 35 C at the best composition. This completes the local temperature map around the top-scoring method and confirms whether the 40 C optimum is bracketed on both sides.

You have shown 40 C is optimal and 45 C is poor at both top compositions; the last missing immediate neighbor is 35 C for the phi0 = 0.15 optimum. This completes the local robustness map around both CRF 1.000 methods.

With CRF 1.000 already secured, use the final injection to fill the one obvious local gap in the successful phi1 = 0.85, 40 C series: phi0 = 0.05 at 16 min. This completes the small response surface around the optimum family and checks whether longer tG plus lower phi0 ever reaches the top plateau.
